articles.title: SJVN Commissions 75 MW Jamui Solar Project as Bihar Crosses 250 MW In Utility Scale Solar in 2026
articles.description: SJVN has achieved the Commercial Operation Date (COD) of the 75 MW Jamui Solar Power Project in Jamui District of Bihar. Bhupender Gupta, Chairman & Managing Director, SJVN, informed that the project has been executed through its subsidiary, SJVN Green Energy Limited (SGEL), adding to its renewable energy portfolio. The project has been developed over approximately 300 acres of outright-purchased land near Village Hadhadiya, Kakanchaur, in Jamui District of Bihar, at an estimated project cost of ₹1,342 crore. The Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency ( BREDA ), Government of Bihar, floated the initial tender for this project. That number will need some explaining from SJVN, which they have not provided at this stage. At this stage, at roughly ₹17.9 crore/MW — against a current Indian utility-scale solar benchmark of roughly ₹3.5–4 crore/MW, that's a 4-5x mismatch. Either the press release number is wrong, it's bundling in something beyond the plant itself, or it's been transposed from a different, larger figure. In 2024, EPC firm Hartek Power Private Limited, had announced the order win from SJVN for a 75 MW (AC) grid-connected solar PV power plant, along with a 132 kV substation, in Jamui, Bihar, valued at Rs 113 crore. Building Solar Project in Bihar at Rs. 1,342 Cr Ajay Sharma, Director (Personnel), SJVN, informed that the 75 MW project is expected to generate approximately 90 million units of electricity during its first year of operation and around 3,522 million units cumulatively over a period of 25 years. Parthajit De, Director (Finance), SJVN, stated that the tariff for the power generated from the project has been fixed at ₹2.96 per unit. The competitive tariff will facilitate the availability of affordable and clean green power to consumers. The electricity generated from the project will be supplied to the State of Bihar. Rajesh Chandel, Director (Projects), SJVN, informed that the project has also contributed to employment generation and local economic development. It has created approximately 15–20 direct employment opportunities and around 5,100 indirect employment opportunities, thereby contributing to the creation of green jobs and providing an economic impetus to the local community. Again, the employment number is off the charts, and needs further explaining from SJVN, sadly absent in the release. That's (5100 indirect jobs) is a large multiplier for a 75 MW plant (SJVN itself cites only 15-20 direct hires). The latest 75 MW commissioning at Jamui, joins BSPGCL's Kajra project in Lakhisarai (via L&T) already commissioned Phase 1 — 185 MW solar + 254 MWh BESS — in February 2026, part of a 301 MW/495 MWh build that's being marketed as India's largest solar-plus-storage project. Marking 2026 as some sort of a breakout year for Bihar's solar pathway, a welcome news from a state that has a long way to go on this road yet.
